messages:
maria: Hey SRE — we got a burn-rate alert for the /generate route last night (around 02:10 UTC). Can someone point me to the dashboard that shows per-route/model burn + latency? Trying to see if this was a blip before asking to mute the alert.

alex: Grafana -> 'SLOs / per-route burn' dashboard. Quick link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/slo-per-route?orgId=1 . Filter on route=/generate and set the time range to 02:00-03:00 UTC. Also check the 'prefix cache hit' panel for the same window.

jonathan: The alert is likely coming from prometheus rule `slo_burn_high` (we tag by route). It uses a 5m eval window atm, which tends to be noisy on bursty traffic. For production routes we usually evaluate over 30m-1h for burn-to-rate.

maria: Is there a runbook for this? I looked in Confluence but couldn't find the exact play.

priya: Runbook is under Observability -> SLOs (Confluence). Quick triage: 1) open grafana link Alex posted 2) check Kibana for request spikes: `route:/generate AND status:5xx OR latency:>2s` 3) check traces (Tempo) for example traces to see upstream failures 4) if <5min spike with no repeated alerts, mark as noisy and propose tuning.

alex: If you want to see raw counts in Prometheus, use the panel same dashboard points at `slo:errors:rate` and `slo:requests:rate`. Also the alert expression we should look at is something like: 

```
# current noisy rule (example)
(sum(increase(slo_error_count{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (route)
 / sum(increase(slo_total_count{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (route)) > 0.05
```
Switching to a longer window reduces false positives: try `[30m]` or `[1h]` and add `for: 10m` to the alert stanza.

jonathan: Example updated rule we tested in staging that looks better: 

```
expr: (sum(increase(slo_error_count{route="/generate"}[1h])) by (route)
 / sum(increase(slo_total_count{route="/generate"}[1h])) by (route)) > 0.03
for: 15m
```
That suppressed a lot of 1-2min blips but still catches real degradations.

maria: Perfect — I'll pull the Grafana snapshots and check traces. If this looks like a one-off spike I'll open a tuning request. Who should I cc on the PR?

priya: cc @alex and @jonathan. If you want ops signoff also CC oncall-tim.

oncall-tim: FYI I saw the alert, briefly paged, then it cleared. No action needed from oncall if you tune to 30m/1h. Happy to review the PR. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — filing a small RFC in the infra-alerts repo with the prometheus change + screenshots. Will ping once draft is ready.

sre-bot: Incident log created: INC-2026-0421-73 (auto) — alert: slo_burn_high route=/generate at 2026-04-21T02:10:23Z.

jonathan: One more tip: if the model backend had a transient restart, you'll see correlated spikes in `backend_restarts_total` on the runtime dashboard. Good to check before tuning the SLO permanently.

maria: Noted. Thanks all — will follow up with the RFC and include the before/after graphs.

alex: Thanks! If you need example PR text lmk, I have a snippet we use for alert changes that includes rationale, metrics, and rollback steps.

maria: Will do — closing this thread for now, will reopen if I need reviewers. :white_check_mark:
